name: Samoa
prevalence_note: On 8 December 2025 the Central Bank of Samoa said commercial banks and money transfer operators had reported a growing number of scams in 2025, mainly after contact on online platforms, and listed parcel, investment, romance, third-party-deposit and online-gaming typologies. It added that in fiscal year 2024/2025 seventy percent of suspicious reports filed by financial institutions with the Bank were scam-related, and that the share was already sixty percent in the early part of 2025/2026.
cross_border_note: The same notice says money placed in a mule account in Samoa is then moved on to the scammer, usually overseas, after separate third parties have been induced to pay in. Approaches are described as coming through WhatsApp or Facebook. A number that merely uses the +685 country code is not proof of a genuine Samoan bank or agency.

scams.name: Third-party deposits into a borrowed Samoan account
scams.name_en: Central Bank of Samoa warning: people are talked into handing over account details, then unused third parties are told to pay into that account, after which the funds are moved on, often overseas
context_keywords: commission for receiving a transfer in Samoa

red_flag_keywords.text: hand over your account so deposits can pass through
keep a commission and forward the rest today
the payer is a separate person who was also misled
move the credit onward as soon as it lands

scams.signals_en: Central Bank of Samoa warns people are offered fast money or commission to lend bank accounts as middlemen: misled third parties deposit funds that are wired onward overseas. CBS and MLPA warn this may be money laundering under Crimes Act.
scams.legit_en: Licensed banks and money-transfer operators in Samoa never ask customers to collect third-party deposits and forward them for a commission. Raise real credit or compliance queries via published channels, not WhatsApp or Facebook.
bait_tactics: Refuse to lend the account or to accept deposits for someone met only online, and say any unusual credit will be raised first with the customer's own bank in Samoa.
Ask why a lawful payment would have to pass through a private account and then leave the country the same day.
Say the approach will be reported to the bank and, if needed, to the Samoa Police Service, and that the chat will not continue.

scams.name: WhatsApp or Facebook investment, prize or fast-money offer
scams.name_en: Central Bank of Samoa warning: contact through WhatsApp or Facebook that pretends to offer prizes, investments or fast-money deals and presses the person to share banking information
context_keywords: unknown sender promising a large in-payment

red_flag_keywords.text: guaranteed high return if you act now
send your bank details to release the prize
unknown person on WhatsApp offering fast money
share passwords or codes to receive the funds

scams.signals_en: Central Bank of Samoa warns of WhatsApp/Facebook prizes, investments and fast-money deals using urgency and pressure, plus emails/calls promising large unknown sums. SamCERT also warns of phishing and fake bank messages.
scams.legit_en: Genuine investments, prizes or bank payments in Samoa are never released only after a private WhatsApp or Facebook chat, and licensed firms never ask for passwords, codes or full account details there. Speak to your own bank first.
bait_tactics: Decline to send banking details or codes in a social-media chat, and say the offer will be checked with the customer's bank or the Central Bank before any money moves.
Ask for a published licence or a callback through the institution's official number, rather than continuing in the same thread.
Break off if the sender keeps pressing for speed or secrecy, and keep a copy of the messages for the bank or Police.
